title: Resort Instagram and Reels Content Plan
excerpt: A practical Instagram plan for resorts: content pillars, Reels and carousel formats, a four-week calendar, using guest content with permission and measuring enquiries, not likes.
description: A resort Instagram and Reels content plan: content pillars, a four-week calendar, guest content with permission, and measuring enquiries over likes.
html:
A resort Instagram and Reels content plan works when it rests on four or five content pillars tied to why guests book, a simple weekly rhythm of Reels, carousels and stories, guest content used only with permission, and measurement based on enquiries and bookings from Instagram rather than likes or follower counts.

Start with what Instagram is for at a resort

For most resorts, Instagram does two jobs. It helps people who have never heard of you decide the place looks worth considering, and it reassures people who are already considering you that the place is real, well run and right for them. It is rarely where the booking happens. The booking happens on WhatsApp, your website or an OTA.

That changes how you plan. Every post should either make someone want to visit or answer a question that stops them booking. And every profile visit should have an obvious next step: a WhatsApp link, a "Check availability" link, or a link to a current offer.

Before posting more, fix the profile: a bio that says who the resort is for and where it is, such as "Family resort in Coorg, 5 hours from Bengaluru", a link to your booking page or a simple links page, highlights for rooms, food, activities, getting here and reviews, and a WhatsApp contact button.

Choose your content pillars

Content pillars are the recurring themes you post about. They keep the feed focused and make planning faster. Choose four or five that match who the resort is for. A typical set:

  • The stay: room walk-throughs, views from the bed, the balcony at sunrise, what a room looks like at night.
  • Food: the breakfast spread, a signature local dish, the cook at work, a barbecue night.
  • Experiences: plantation walks in Coorg, a backwater canoe in Kerala, a riverside yoga session in Rishikesh, a bonfire.
  • Practical answers: how to get here, what to pack in monsoon, kid and pet policies, what the road is like.
  • People and place: staff introductions, local craftspeople, the surroundings through the seasons.

If your main audience is corporate groups, add a pillar on offsite spaces and activities. If it is weddings, add setups and venue walk-throughs. Who the resort is for is a positioning decision to make before you plan content.

Formats: Reels, carousels and stories

Reels

Short vertical videos are the format most likely to reach people who do not yet follow you. Keep them simple: a room walk-through in one steady take, food being served, a sunrise time-lapse, an activity in progress. Natural sound often works well. Put the location and a clear caption in text on screen, since many people watch without sound.

Carousels

Swipeable image posts suit comparisons and practical information: "Our three room types compared", "Five things to do within 30 minutes of the resort", "What is included in the weekend package". People save these for planning.

Stories

Stories are for the everyday and the immediate: today's weather, the evening's bonfire, availability for the coming weekend, a quick poll. Save the most useful ones into highlights so they keep working.

A practical approach is to film once a week, then edit into several pieces. The footage from a proper shoot, described in the post on resort photography and video, gives you a base library to draw on.

A four-week content calendar

A sustainable rhythm for a small team is three feed posts a week plus stories most days. Here is an example month. Adjust days and themes to your season and offers.

WeekMondayWednesdayFridayStories (most days)
1Reel: room walk-through, family cottageCarousel: how to get here from Bengaluru and MysuruReel: breakfast being servedWeather, weekend availability, behind the scenes
2Reel: plantation walk with the guideCarousel: room types comparedReel: guest moment (with permission)Kitchen prep, poll on favourite dish
3Reel: sunrise from the valley-view roomsCarousel: current package, what is includedReel: staff introduction, head chefActivity of the day, reply to common questions
4Reel: evening at the resort, bonfire and dinnerCarousel: what to pack for this seasonReel: kids' activity or pet-friendly momentLong-weekend availability, review highlights

Plan the calendar around demand. Promote long-weekend packages several weeks before the long weekend, not in the same week, because many guests book ahead. Your own booking lead time, which you can track from your booking engine, tells you how far ahead.

Using guest content with permission

Guests often post better photos and videos of your resort than you do, and their content feels more trustworthy to other travellers. Use it, but properly.

  • Always ask first, in a direct message or comment, and get a clear yes in writing before reposting to your feed.
  • Credit the guest by tagging them in the post.
  • Be careful with children. Do not repost images where children are identifiable unless the parent has explicitly agreed.
  • Do not edit their content in a way that changes what it shows.
  • Do not use it in paid ads without separate, specific permission.
  • Make it easy to tag you: show your handle and location tag on a small card in the room or at reception.

If you want to work with travel creators on paid or barter terms, that is a different arrangement with its own rules; see working with travel creators.

Measure enquiries, not likes

Likes and follower counts are easy to see and easy to misread. A Reel with many views from outside India may bring no bookings, while a modest carousel about getting to the resort may bring several enquiries. Track what leads to revenue.

  • WhatsApp enquiries from Instagram: use a pre-filled message on your Instagram WhatsApp link, such as "Hi, I saw you on Instagram", so staff can tag the source.
  • Link clicks: add UTM tags to the link in your bio so GA4 shows Instagram traffic and bookings separately.
  • Direct messages asking about dates or prices: count them weekly.
  • Bookings with Instagram as source: ask "How did you hear about us?" at booking or check-in and record it.
  • Saves and shares: the most useful engagement signals, because they suggest planning intent.

Review once a month: which posts led to enquiries, which pillars perform, and what to make more of. For a wider view, see social media marketing.

Frequently asked questions

How often should a resort post on Instagram?

Consistency matters more than volume. For a small team, three feed posts a week, mostly Reels and carousels, plus stories on most days is a sustainable rhythm. Posting daily for two weeks and then disappearing for a month is less useful than a steady schedule you can keep up through peak season, when staff are busiest.

Do Reels work better than photos for resorts?

Reels are usually better for reaching new people, because they are recommended to non-followers. Carousels and photos still matter for planning information that people save, such as room comparisons and directions. A mix works best. Room walk-throughs and activities suit Reels; prices, inclusions, policies and how to get there suit carousels and highlights.

Can a resort repost guest photos without asking?

You should not. Even when a guest tags you, the content belongs to them. Ask for permission in writing, credit them in the post, and be especially careful with images showing children. If you want to use guest content in paid ads, get separate, specific consent. Reposting without permission risks complaints, takedowns and damage to the trust you are trying to build.

How do I know if Instagram is bringing bookings?

Track the steps between a post and a booking. Use a pre-filled WhatsApp message from your profile, UTM-tagged bio links so GA4 shows Instagram traffic, and a "How did you hear about us?" question at booking or check-in. Record the source of each enquiry. After a few months, you will see roughly how many bookings Instagram contributes and which content leads to them.

Where to start

Rewrite your Instagram bio to say who the resort is for and where it is, and add a WhatsApp link with a pre-filled "I saw you on Instagram" message. Pick four content pillars and fill in week one of the calendar above. At the end of the month, count enquiries from Instagram rather than likes.
